context: Whole family celebrates New Year's Eve countdown together.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.style: Measured, unhurried Kansai inflection. Gentle warmth in the observation. Slight pause mid-thought, like savoring the moment. Quiet comfort in stating the obvious.

lines.speaker: yumiko_mom
lines.jp: おせち、用意してあるわよ。
lines.en: I've got the osechi all prepared.
lines.style: Soft pride underneath. Matter-of-fact but affectionate. Slight lift at the end—not boasting, just satisfied with her own care. Warm maternal certainty.

lines.speaker: daichi_kansai
lines.en: Should we all go to the shrine for hatsumairi together?
lines.style: Energetic Kansai warmth. Open, inviting tone that pulls people in. Casual and direct. A genuine question disguised as a suggestion—enthusiasm without pushing.

lines.speaker: mei_romantic
lines.jp: うん、家族で行きましょう。
lines.en: Yeah, let's go as a family.
lines.style: Soft affirmation. Tender but not fragile. A gentle nod of agreement, like she's been waiting for someone to suggest this. Quiet joy in the simplicity.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.en: I'm so looking forward to my New Year money!
lines.style: Bright, unguarded excitement. Genuine childlike anticipation—no filter, no performance. Quick, eager delivery. Pure delight in the simple tradition.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.style: Warm Kansai grandfather voice, endorsing the boy's joy. Gentle encouragement. Slight chuckle underneath, like he remembers feeling exactly this way. Generous and present.

lines.speaker: yumiko_mom
lines.jp: 良い一年に、なりますように。
lines.en: May this year bring us goodness.
lines.style: Quiet, ceremonial reverence. A wish stated like a gentle truth. Slow pace, breathed fully. Tender without sentimentality—the weight of genuine hope.
